architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept transfer of the H-CORE benchmark to S1C02 if the repeat-mean SI_15_60 is between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive, corresponding to 9.51% ± the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: A repeat-mean SI_15_60 below 7.51% falsifies the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction as transferable to S1C02 because it is more than 2.00 percentage points below 9.51%. A value from 7.51% through 11.51% falsifies none of H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL. A value above 11.51% is inconsistent with the numerical H-CORE prediction but does not meet the registry's specified below-prediction falsification condition. No outcome from this unmodified candidate can falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C02::M-REPEAT with three controlled and fully recorded preparations to test whether realization-state variability can account for the failed transfer before interpreting any modifier experiment.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Arithmetic mean across at least two independent preparations of SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C, in percent.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 is the strongest scientifically defensible identified card: it directly measures the unresolved failure coordinate and establishes whether the E1-derived reactive-core benchmark transfers to the central E2 core. It is not a mitigation formulation and cannot answer the acrylic-only question, so it is committed only as a narrow discriminating probe of H-CORE benchmark transfer.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer's selection of S1C02 over the tied reactive-core cards because it is the registered central E2 anchor and lacks a thermal-hold trajectory. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: this card has zero registered pairwise discrimination and cannot test or falsify H-RESIN or H-DUAL. I did not follow the Robustness Adjudicator's preferred acrylic-only intervention because no valid candidate identifier or complete experiment card for it is supplied, and fabricating one would violate the selection contract. I also rejected the Proposer/VOI card's modifier-mechanism claims and replaced the invalid 4.75% resin threshold with the H-CORE transfer threshold defined by 9.51% and the 2.00 percentage-point measurement resolution.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 °C (thermal-hold drift).
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run measured a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C, compared with 9.51% for E1 over the same window; each profile currently has only one measured run.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The temperature coordinate is represented by multiple six-point 80–130 °C sweeps, and realized viscosity variability is directly documented for E2 with three runs and 2.80–3.57-fold max/min spread. In contrast, isothermal behavior is represented only by one four-point 120 °C hold run each for E1 and E5, with no repeated hold estimate, no measured E2 reactive-core hold trajectory, and no modifier-axis comparison.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity during a 120 °C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage, without requiring an absolute viscosity unit.
Use at least two independent preparations or hold repeats so the matched-window drift can be judged against the declared 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.
Record and control preparation and thermal history because E2 temperature sweeps show large realization-scale variability.
Select an acrylic-like-only candidate with zero minor tackifier-like content so a low-drift result can directly test the tackifier-required prediction of H-DUAL.
Compute the prospective H-CORE benchmark E1_drift × phi_r from the inspected composition and freeze it before observing the new result.
Compare the measured drift with both the linear-dilution benchmark and the H-RESIN threshold of less than half that benchmark; do not extrapolate beyond the measured 120 °C, 15–60 min window.
Include a realized-viscosity anchor or matched-temperature viscosity reading for the same preparation so drift suppression is not confused with an uncontrolled displacement of the viscosity level.
planner.scientific_question: At a controlled reactive mass fraction, does an acrylic-like-only modification reduce the 15–60 min viscosity drift at 120 °C substantially below the E1-based linear-dilution prediction, or does low drift require activation of the minor tackifier-like axis? A drift below half the linear prediction would support H-RESIN while falsifying H-CORE and H-DUAL; drift near the linear prediction would be consistent with H-CORE or H-DUAL and would falsify H-RESIN.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 4.75% across at least two repeats would falsify the E1-based H-CORE linear-scaling prediction for this reactive-core anchor and would also contradict the broad tackifier-required condition in H-DUAL. Because S1C02 contains neither resin axis, it would not establish the resin-suppression mechanism H-RESIN; instead it would show that the E1 drift coefficient does not transfer as the assumed universal reactive-core benchmark.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: Drift at or above 9.51% would be consistent with the H-CORE benchmark for this unmodified core. It would not validly falsify H-RESIN or distinguish H-CORE from H-DUAL because no acrylic-like or minor-tackifier-like intervention is present.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 4.75% and 9.51%, or repeat variability that prevents resolution at the declared 2 percentage-point threshold, would indicate partial benchmark transfer or unresolved process-state effects. It would not adjudicate the modifier mechanisms.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It directly measures drift but largely repeats the existing E1 hold observation used to define the 9.51% benchmark, while S1C02 fills the explicitly missing E2-anchor hold trajectory.
It has the same zero pairwise discrimination and direct measurement quality as S1C02, but it is not the registered central E2 reactive-core anchor.
It has the same component vector but uses an interpolated reactive core rather than the measured E2 anchor, weakening baseline interpretability.
It controls realization-scale variability but does not observe the thermal-hold drift coordinate on which H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL disagree.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 is the only displayed measurement that directly observes the declared failure mode without a model fit and within the supported 120 C, 15-60 min window. S1C02 is scientifically preferable within the tied set because E2 is the registered central reactive-core anchor and currently has no hold data. However, this no-modifier experiment has zero registered pairwise discrimination and cannot answer the planner's acrylic-only question; no acrylic-only experiment card or candidate identity is supplied among the displayed contenders.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All nine displayed hold cards have the same VOI score and component vector and predict 9.51% under every registered hypothesis, so none provides pairwise hypothesis discrimination. S1C02 is preferred because it is the measured E2 reactive-core anchor identified by the tool trace, lies within the characterized local chemistry, and lacks any thermal-hold trajectory. Measuring it therefore closes a specifically documented baseline uncertainty, whereas S1C01 would mainly repeat the already observed E1 reference and the remaining tied cards are other core perturbations or interpolations.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace S1C02 as the primary intervention with an E2-proportioned acrylic-like-only candidate in the supported 15-20% initial band, with TK100 fixed at 0%, while running S1C02 as a contemporaneous process-matched control. No identifier for such an acrylic-only candidate is supplied in the payload, so a valid catalog candidate ID cannot be selected without fabrication. Preserve the matched 120 C, 15-60 min hold measurement, use independently prepared replicates, record preparation and thermal history, include a same-preparation 120 C viscosity anchor, verify modifier reactivity and true stoichiometry, and predefine repeat aggregation and uncertainty.
residual_decision_risk: The decision-stability metrics and flip boundaries are withheld, so quantitative sensitivity to weight perturbations cannot be adjudicated.
No catalog identifier or complete formulation card for the preferred acrylic-like-only E2-based candidate is supplied.
Modifier reactivity and true NCO:OH stoichiometry remain unverified.
E2 has shown a 3.57-fold realized-viscosity spread at 120 C, and M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state.
The supplied protocol does not define repeat aggregation or treatment of discordant or borderline repeats relative to the 2 percentage-point resolution.
The E1-derived linear-dilution benchmark may not transfer directly to the E2 core because core composition and NCO:OH differ.
The acrylic analogue evidence supports only a coarse candidate region and does not establish a local mechanism or exact optimum.
Conclusions remain limited to formulation-level rheology over the measured 120 C, 15-60 min window.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 is useful for testing transfer of the E1-derived drift benchmark to the E2 reactive core, but it cannot answer the stated acrylic-only mechanistic question: AC1920 and TK100 are both zero, and H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL all predict 9.51%, leaving every registered pair unseparated. A low result would challenge transfer of the E1 benchmark rather than establish resin suppression, while a high result could not falsify H-RESIN because no resin-modified composition was tested. The preferred primary experiment is therefore M-HOLD-120 on a process-matched E2-based formulation containing 15-20% acrylic-like modifier and zero minor tackifier, with S1C02 retained as a contemporaneous no-modifier control. This is a change in experiment selection, not merely a restriction on interpretation.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The supplied decision-stability report is explicitly withheld, so top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary are unavailable. Therefore no numerical perturbation or smallest scaling that changes the tied top set can be identified. Among the displayed cards, S1C02::M-HOLD-120 shares the top VOI score and component vector with eight other reactive-core hold cards. Scientifically, giving greater priority to hypothesis_discrimination or intervention sufficiency, rather than minimizing perturbation size first, is defensible because the stated question concerns an acrylic-like-only intervention and all displayed top cards have zero pairwise discrimination. The payload does not provide enough information to determine the exact weight scaling at which an acrylic-only card would become top ranked.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol can physically measure SI_15_60 below 4.75% or at/above 9.51%, and therefore can test whether the E1-derived benchmark transfers to E2. It cannot, however, meet the registered falsification conditions for H-RESIN or H-DUAL because S1C02 is neither resin-modified nor acrylic-only. Those portions of the stated criterion are logically inapplicable even if the numerical threshold is reached.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that this experiment selects among H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL would be unsupported; at most it measures whether the E1-derived 9.51% benchmark transfers to the E2 reactive core.
objections.objection: The proposed experiment S1C02::M-HOLD-120 activates neither registered modifier axis: AC1920 = 0.0%, TK100 = 0.0%, and reactive_mass_fraction = 1.0000. Consequently, hypothesis_discrimination_detail assigns the same 9.51% prediction to H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, with score 0.0 and no separated pairs. It therefore cannot answer the planner's stated acrylic-only question or discriminate any registered hypothesis pair. The Proposer correctly declares hypotheses_separated = [] and lists all three under hypotheses_not_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low or high drift could be misattributed to H-RESIN, H-DUAL, or universal H-CORE scaling when it may instead reflect E1-to-E2 core composition, stoichiometry, or preparation-state differences.
objections.objection: The 9.51% benchmark comes from E1, but S1C02 is the E2 core. Relative to E1, E2 changes NCO:OH from 1.7 to 1.8 and MDI fraction from 0.19287 to 0.20191, with corresponding polyol-fraction changes. Thus a deviation from 9.51% cannot be attributed to modifier-mediated dilution or resin suppression because no modifier is present and the reactive-core stoichiometry/composition also differs. In addition, M-HOLD-120 is marked controls_process_state = false, while E2 has a documented 3.57-fold realized-viscosity spread at 120 C; the displayed protocol does not implement the planner's required realized-viscosity anchor or specify the six missing process fields.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The drift measurement remains directly interpretable, but borderline or discordant repeats could be classified inconsistently.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 at 120 C, with no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. However, the protocol does not define how the two repeat values are combined or what 'across at least two repeats' means statistically relative to the declared 2 percentage-point resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Numerically attainable outcomes would be treated as falsifying modifier hypotheses that were never experimentally instantiated.
objections.objection: The displayed falsification criterion is not valid for all hypotheses it names. It says H-RESIN is falsified at drift >= 9.51%, but the H-RESIN registry condition applies 'at a resin-modified composition'; S1C02 has no resin-like modifier. It also says H-DUAL is falsified if 'this acrylic-only composition' reaches low drift, but S1C02 is not acrylic-only—it contains 0.0% acrylic. The instrument can numerically observe drift below 4.75% or at/above 9.51%, so transfer of the E1 benchmark is testable, but those outcomes cannot satisfy the registered H-RESIN or H-DUAL falsification conditions. The Proposer's outcome_interpretation correctly retreats from those invalid claims, creating a conflict with the card-level acceptance and falsification language.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A direct rheological observation on an unmodified core would be overextended into evidence for a resin-suppression mechanism that the experiment cannot establish.
objections.objection: No target-validation identity, follow-up result, or outcome-derived label is visibly used, so no outcome leakage is evident. The hypothesis registry also explicitly limits claims to formulation-level rheology. Nevertheless, the card-level acceptance_criterion states that drift below 4.75% 'accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE' even though S1C02 contains no resin and cannot establish the proposed resin mechanism of reduced effective concentration or encounter frequency. The Proposer's later outcome interpretation correctly states that such a result would only challenge transfer of the E1 drift coefficient.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace S1C02 with a controlled acrylic-like-only formulation based on the E2 core, with nonzero acrylic in the supported 15-20% initial band and TK100 fixed at 0%, while preserving the normalized E2 core proportions and verifying modifier reactivity/true stoichiometry. Run M-HOLD-120 on that formulation and a contemporaneous E2 no-modifier control using independently prepared, process-matched replicates; record the missing preparation and thermal-history fields and include a same-preparation 120 C viscosity anchor. Predefine repeat aggregation and uncertainty. This would directly test whether acrylic alone produces drift below half of the appropriate linear-dilution benchmark and could separate H-DUAL from the alternatives.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02 activates neither modifier axis and gives identical 9.51% predictions for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, so it has zero registered pairwise discrimination and cannot answer the stated acrylic-only mechanistic question.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This must be obtained first to load the upstream material-state structure, state-shift behavior, calibration evidence, and design rules before any candidate or experiment ranking is admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: The evidence-derived candidate axes, E2 reactive-core anchor, and historical claim boundary are needed to identify an admissible acrylic-only mechanistic probe without treating the candidate lattice as a discovered optimum.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: The composition of the registered reactive-core anchor is needed to calculate candidate reactive mass fractions and the prospective H-CORE linear-dilution prediction.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: E1 supplies the least-drifting original reference, so its composition is needed to interpret whether its hold behavior is a suitable reactive-core benchmark or includes modifier axes.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: E5 establishes the severe local drift observation; its composition is needed to determine which chemistry axes accompany that failure without assigning causality from formulation identity alone.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The full measured E1 trajectory and deterministic descriptors are needed to freeze the reference drift and assess trajectory shape within the supported time window.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The full measured high-drift trajectory is needed to characterize the observed failure and compare candidate measurement plans on the same 120 °C matched window.

tool_trace.name: get_repeatability_risk
tool_trace.reason: The measured preparation-to-preparation viscosity spread is needed to specify state controls and avoid interpreting one nominal viscosity level as an intrinsic formulation property.

tool_trace.name: get_temperature_support
tool_trace.reason: Measured support and response summaries are needed to keep any viscosity anchor inside the local temperature domain and to assess whether 120 °C is supported for the reactive-core reference.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied acrylic-like digest is empty, so source-level analogue evidence and its limitations are needed before choosing among sparsely covered acrylic-only candidates.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied minor-tackifier digest is empty, so source-level evidence is needed to assess the prior basis for the tackifier-required hypothesis and the bounded tackifier axis.

voi_sent_to_model.note: The deterministic decision policy for this run is the stated rule ORDER. Experiments are presented in that order. Component vectors are unchanged facts.
voi_sent_to_model.order_description: perturbation size is minimized before intervention sufficiency is assessed

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 4.75%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
